thread:
nora.p: hi folks — I was on paid parental leave during open enrollment and apparently missed the window. I need to enroll in medical + dental starting now. Is there a late enrollment path for folks on approved parental leave?

people-ops: welcome back! We do have a process for employees who miss OE due to approved leave. Short version: you can request a late enrollment exception; HR reviews, benefits may approve administratively. We'll need docs showing you were on approved leave during OE.

nora.p: thanks. My leave was approved 2026-11-01 through 2027-02-28 (LOA request ID LOA-8271). OE window closed 2026-11-15. I was out the entire OE window. I want coverage effective 2027-01-01 if possible.

leave-admin: confirm — LOA-8271 shows approved paid parental leave from 2026-11-01 to 2027-02-28. Good to include that LOA ID when you submit the exception request.

benefits-ops: procedure:
1) Submit "Late Enrollment Exception" form in Workday Benefits (select reason = "missed OE due to approved leave").
2) Attach LOA approval email and any confirmation screenshots from leave-admin.
3) Specify requested effective date (we'll check carrier rules).

Note: carriers treat OE misses differently. Some carriers allow administrative late adds to the start of the plan year (2027-01-01) when the employee was on approved leave; others only allow mid-month effective dates after approval. We'll escalate on receipt.

nora.p: ok I'm attaching LOA docs now. Would premiums be backdated to 1/1 or start the first of the month after approval? Also will payroll take a catch-up?

payroll-bot: payroll rules: if benefits approves a retro effective 2027-01-01, payroll will collect the missed employee share via a catch-up deduction on the next payroll run after benefits confirmation. If the effective date is the first of the month after approval (e.g., 2027-03-01), deductions will start on the payroll covering that date. We can do voluntary spreads for catch-up if you prefer smaller increments; request that in your ticket.

benefits-ops: received your exception request and LOA docs (REQ-2387654321). We're sending a formal request to carriers today for medical + dental. Estimated carrier response 5-10 business days. If carrier approves retro to 2027-01-01, we'll push to payroll for reconciliation.

eric.m: curious — any precedent on whether carriers approve OE exceptions for parental leave? We had a similar case last year and the major medical carrier allowed retro. Dental denied retro but allowed add effective first of next month.

benefits-ops: @eric.m correct. Historically Redwood Health (medical) has been willing to approve admin retro for approved LOA cases; dental carriers vary. We'll request medical retro to 2027-01-01 and dental retro to 2027-01-01 but note that dental may only allow 2027-03-01 effective depending on policy.

nora.p: understood. If dental only allows 3/1 I might get private dental in the interim. Any documentation I should prepare to speed approvals?

people-ops: best items to include:
- LOA approval email or Workday LOA ID
- Screenshot of OE confirmation stating you were not active during OE (optional)
- Brief note describing inability to access enrollment while on leave

Also mark the request "expedite" in Workday if you need faster turnaround for care.

benefits-ops: update: carrier responses — medical (Redwood Health) approved retro effective 2027-01-01. Dental carrier denied retro but approved enrollment effective 2027-03-01. We've queued payroll reconciliation. Expected payroll catch-up on next monthly pay after benefits posts (approx 2027-04-15 payroll).

nora.p: thanks!! For the dental gap I'll enroll in a standalone short-term plan — any company resource list for recommended short-term dental vendors?

people-ops: we don't endorse outside vendors but can share a list of commonly used short-term plans other employees have used; DM me and I'll share. Also if you want payroll to spread the catch-up over N pay periods, reply here with preferred N and we'll coordinate with payroll.

nora.p: please spread over 3 pay periods if possible. Also thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Really appreciate the help while juggling new baby & paperwork :heart:
